requiredExport: saved world or exact record snapshot

why: An appropriation permits spending but supplies neither cash nor service.
A commitment chooses a saved operating or maintenance plan.
A completed installment moves money to its recorded recipient.
Operating payment counts authored contracted service hours; maintenance payment requires a later counted restoration outturn.
Payment purpose and the saved physical consequence determine the effect; a transfer alone cannot establish a ride.
conditions: Requires legal authority, posted installment and completed transfer.
Operating and maintenance consequences are distinct.
Authored contract costs and capacity units are game-profile data, not researched effect-size estimates.
reverseOnRepeal: Repeal may close future authority according to operative law and existing commitment rules; it does not undo a completed transfer or erase delivered service.
who: Recorded government payer and recipient organization. No named rider is proved by these four exported records.
lagWhy: Operating service uses the posted payment date; the authored maintenance alternative has a 90-day delivery lead, which must be checked against the saved commitment.

effectSizing.reason: This is accounting/attribution evidence, not a new empirical coefficient; no inferred size or CI.
